title: Family coordination — illustrative prompt wall
summary: The supplied notes cluster around fragmented discovery, manual capture, and fragile attention; a paper-first preference remains separate.
limitations: Illustrative demo built from user-provided benchmark notes; P-labels are prompt identifiers, not verified participants or human-interview evidence.
This small supplied set cannot establish prevalence or represent families generally.

clusters.label: The change hides in the channel
clusters.description: Schedule information is distributed before anyone can reconcile it.

notes.text: P-001 checks three school apps every morning.
P-002 relies on text messages from another parent.
P-003 missed a practice change posted only in email.

clusters.label: People build memory scaffolds
clusters.description: The formal calendar competes with screenshots and personal workarounds.

notes.text: P-004 says the shared calendar is accurate but nobody checks it.
P-005 screenshots messages to remember them.
P-006 says one caregiver enters everything while others assume it is handled.

clusters.label: Attention—not change—is fragile
clusters.description: Noise and late discovery cause failure, while the counterexample says change is manageable when seen.

notes.text: P-007 gets duplicate alerts and ignores most of them.
P-008 learned about a cancellation after arriving.
P-010 says last-minute changes are manageable when the right person sees them.

outliers.text: P-009 likes paper on the refrigerator.
